FeCoNiCr0.6Al0.4 HEA was prepared by vacuum arc melting using raw materials with a purity greater than 99.95%, and argon as the flux gas.
The melted FeCoNiCr0.6Al0.4 alloy ingots were homogenized for six hours at 1200 °C, water quenched, and then cold rolled to 66% volume reduction.
The melted FeCoNiCr0.6Al0.4 alloy ingots were homogenized for six hours at 1200 °C, water quenched, and then cold rolled to 66% volume reduction.
To relieve internal stresses and fully recrystallize the cold rolled sheets, they are recrystallized at 1200 °C for five minutes.

The recrystallized samples were then heat treated at 600, 700, 800, and 900 °C for 24 h, followed by water quenching. For ease of description, these alloys are labeled A-600, A-700, A-800, and A-900, respectively.

At an aging temperature of 600 °C, only a simple face-centered cubic (FCC) structure is observed.
When the aging temperature is 700 °C, the characteristic peak of (110)BCC begins to appear near the characteristic peak of (111)FCC in the alloy.
The spherical particles precipitated in the bright region inside the grain are L12 phase rich in Ni and Al elements.
Combined with the XRD analysis, it can be seen that the precipitation phases at the grain boundaries of both A-700 and A-800 alloys are B2 phases enriched with Ni and Al elements.
With the aging temperature increasing to 900 °C, a large number of Ni-Al rich B2 phase disappeared at the grain boundary of the alloy. At the same time, the Cr-rich phase begin to form.
